incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using AI-generated images to impersonate him, offering fraudulent immigration services such as US residency assistance for $2,200. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, though suspicious activity first appeared last October. The situation has dramatically escalated over the past three months.

The scams typically begin with social media videos directing people to contact phone numbers through WhatsApp, where fraudsters exchange emails and send fake contracts. An anti-piracy company hired by Leal's office has successfully removed approximately 6,500 fake profiles across platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Leal warns immigrants to be cautious of requests for payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App and advises verifying anyone offering legal services online. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scheme's origin.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake online article featuring ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler and Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock discussing a fraudulent cryptocurrency platform called Boulder Sparhaven has become a prominent example of AI-generated investment scams. The fabricated interview, which never occurred, depicted an increasingly heated conversation where Bullock allegedly stormed out over Kohler's questions about the unlicensed trading platform. This type of scam is rising rapidly, with Australian Securities and Investments Commission research showing that deepfake images and videos of celebrities and politicians are becoming more prevalent and convincing thanks to artificial intelligence technology.

ASIC removed 19,400 scams last year, representing a 182 percent increase, including a 279 percent jump in phishing scams and a 151 percent increase in fake investment platforms. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, along with politicians and financial figures like Pauline Hanson and Tom Piotrowski, top the list of commonly impersonated Australians. Scammers create elaborate webs of deception using fake news articles, fabricated testimonials, and advertisements to lure investors, often followed by scripted phone calls and small payments to build trust. ASIC recommends verifying Australian Financial Services licence numbers through official registers before investing.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A proposed class-action lawsuit filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco on Thursday accuses smart ring maker Oura of false advertising regarding its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit claims that Oura's rings, which cost $300 and up, cannot accurately measure sleep stages as advertised, instead relying on artificial intelligence predictions no better than guessing. The lawsuit alleges that Oura marketed its products with claims such as 95% sleep staging accuracy compared to clinical sleep labs, but lacks the complex medical equipment required for such measurements. Oura built an $11 billion company on consumer trust, according to the filing.

Oura responded by defending its science and peer-reviewed research, stating that its devices estimate sleep stages using multiple physiological signals and have been validated against polysomnography standards. The company argues that while its rings are not medical devices or substitutes for clinical studies, they provide valuable estimates. The lawsuit seeks class action status and a jury trial, though it remains unclear what compensation affected customers might receive if the case succeeds. This marks another legal challenge for Oura, which faces a separate ongoing lawsuit over alleged collection of sensitive personal information without consent.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified the Aurora ransomware group operating since April 2026, targeting organizations across multiple countries. The group developed a Linux variant of their ransomware capable of attacking ESXi virtualization environments. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten target organizations. The ESXi ransomware uses ChaCha20 encryption and includes a special mode to encrypt only virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands.

Researchers also discovered the Aurora group employed a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for ESXi hosts and vCenter servers. A second cluster of suspected Aurora activity was identified in eight victim organizations across multiple countries, using different attack methods including SQL Server exploitation and data exfiltration to S3 storage. The investigation revealed the attackers were careful to avoid certain actions like account lockouts and DCSync attacks, suggesting operational discipline within the group.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut restaurants across the Northeast, filed a lawsuit in Texas Business Court alleging that Pizza Hut's mandatory adoption of Dragontail, an AI-powered delivery management system, caused over $100 million in damages. Before the 2024 rollout, Chaac maintained over 90% on-time delivery rates and double-digit sales growth. The system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, causing drivers to wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple orders together, significantly delaying deliveries and reducing customer satisfaction. In New York City alone, year-over-year sales swung from positive 10.19% to negative 9.78% after implementation.

Chaac claims Pizza Hut breached their franchise agreement by mandating the incompatible software without adequate training or support, and failed to exercise reasonable business judgment when warned about declining performance metrics. The franchisee is seeking over $100 million in damages plus attorneys' fees. Pizza Hut stated it is reviewing the lawsuit claims and will respond through legal channels. The lawsuit emerges as Pizza Hut's parent company, Yum! Brands, explores strategic options for the struggling brand and plans to close 250 US locations this year.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and Fresh Air staff members to defraud people by offering fake interview opportunities. Authors, entertainers and public figures have received personalized emails claiming to represent the NPR show, with detailed references to their work and proposed topics. The scheme eventually asks victims to pay fees for production costs, with some targets also solicited for social media login credentials. Misericordia University history professor Jennifer Black received such an email and grew suspicious when asked to pay $250, noting the communication seemed to come from Gross herself rather than production staff.

Cybersecurity experts say artificial intelligence has made these social engineering scams more convincing and personalized than traditional fraud attempts. WHYY, NPR and Fresh Air have confirmed the fraudulent emails and are investigating with law enforcement. The organizations state they never charge guests for interviews and warn that any fee request should be considered illegitimate. Red flags include requests for money and emails from unprofessional addresses like terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com. Experts recommend verifying interview invitations through official organization contacts rather than responding to suspicious messages.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
A fake American think tank funded by Israel published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in just nine days, designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots to generate pro-Israel arguments. The Hanover Institute for Public Policy, which does not exist as a legal entity and has no staff or physical address, presented arguments on topics including Palestinian torture, Israeli war crimes, and Gaza's food supply as neutral research. The operation used a commercial platform specifically designed to optimize content so that AI systems like ChatGPT and Perplexity would cite it. A New York media company called Piro Inc registered the site with the US justice department under foreign agent disclosure laws.

The broader campaign, financed by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government through intermediaries like the advertising firm Havas Media, aimed to manipulate how chatbots respond to user questions. Research shows Israel's approval among Americans has dropped significantly, with only 36 percent sympathizing with Israel in recent polling and 60 percent viewing it unfavorably. Israeli officials have expressed doubts about the campaign's effectiveness, with some calling it a failure despite substantial spending. Experts warn that such artificial intelligence manipulation represents a growing threat, as poisoned training data may influence chatbot responses without users being able to verify sources.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records have filed separate lawsuits against AI music generators Udio and Suno, accusing them of illegally copying thousands of copyrighted songs without permission. The labels claim both companies scraped massive amounts of music to train their AI models and are now generating songs that directly reproduce sections of famous recordings. The lawsuits were filed in New York against Udio and Massachusetts against Suno, and the companies have refused to disclose which music they trained on, claiming instead that their use constitutes fair use.

To support their case, the record labels demonstrated they could repeatedly recreate versions of famous copyrighted songs by using targeted prompts describing specific decades, genres, and artists. Examples include generating songs resembling Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Goode," Green Day's "American Idiot," and Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You." The labels submitted a thumb drive of AI-generated music as evidence and provided a lengthy list of thousands of specific copyrighted works from artists like The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, Bruce Springsteen, and Madonna that they claim were used to train the models without authorization.

Under the settlement, Udio has agreed to launch a new platform next year using only authorized and licensed music, allowing users to customize and share compositions. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Udio said artists can opt into the platform and receive compensation, though specific details remain unclear. This represents Udio's first major licensing agreement with a record label. The company also announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

State Farm's defense lawyers apologized for using artificial intelligence that generated fake legal cases in their filings for a lawsuit brought by Los Angeles homeowner Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga. The plaintiff's attorneys discovered that State Farm's motions contained seven nonexistent case citations across eight filings, along with fake quotes and holdings. Lawyer Jacquelene Robinson admitted she used an AI tool called Irys, which she mistakenly believed would perform accuracy checks on legal citations. The case involves Meni-Siliga's home in Carson, which became uninhabitable after a 2020 fire, with subsequent water damage during repairs. She claims State Farm delayed approving repairs, leaving her home incomplete and forcing her family into bankruptcy and foreclosure. The trial is scheduled for October.

The incident highlights growing concerns about artificial intelligence in the legal profession, with 41 percent of law firms now using generative AI. A database tracking legal hallucinations worldwide has documented 1,922 cases, mostly in the United States. Last year, a California attorney received a record ten thousand dollar fine for submitting a brief with twenty-one fabricated quotes. State Farm stated it expects its external legal counsel to maintain the highest ethical standards and verify all filings' accuracy.

stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Headline: What We Know About Haryana Police's AI Task Force.
stories.Summary:
Haryana Police is establishing an Artificial Intelligence Task Force to expand AI use in law enforcement operations. An Indian Police Service officer will lead the initiative, which focuses on cybercrime investigations, financial transaction analysis, complaint management and court information processing. The police emphasized that AI will support human investigators rather than replace them, with officers responsible for verifying leads and making final decisions.

The task force will build on existing technology systems Haryana Police already uses, including a 2022 facial recognition program that deactivated nearly 1,000 fraudulent SIM cards and current cybercrime helplines. The police plan to implement safeguards around accuracy, transparency, data security and human oversight, though specific implementation details remain unclear. Haryana Police has not disclosed how it will test systems, measure errors, conduct audits or handle incorrect results, and has not explained how new AI capabilities will integrate with current infrastructure or whether it plans to use facial recognition or predictive policing technologies.

stories.Headline: 《TAIPEI TIMES》 Taiwan aims to train 500,000 AI pros by 2040 - 焦點
stories.Summary:
Taiwan's government plans to invest over 40 billion Taiwan dollars, approximately 1.26 billion US dollars, to develop 10 major artificial intelligence projects next year. President William Lai has set an ambitious goal to train at least 500,000 AI professionals by 2040. The administration launched the AI Talent Ark Project this year to nurture talent through fundamental education, professional development, and data-driven approaches, aiming to build a large AI talent pool and strengthen Taiwan's competitiveness in technology sectors.

The government is also prioritizing technological sovereignty and national resilience. The Minister of Digital Affairs announced plans to accumulate at least 10,000 graphics processing units through private investment in AI computing centers within a year. Taiwan is focusing on developing sovereign AI systems that understand Taiwanese perspectives and languages, along with low-Earth-orbit satellite communications to ensure independent communication capabilities. Officials emphasized that technological sovereignty means focusing on critical technologies rather than developing every technology domestically.

stories.Headline: CSA's Top Cloud Threats: Identity, AI -- Campus Technology
stories.Summary:
The Cloud Security Alliance surveyed 507 security professionals to identify the top threats to cloud computing in 2026. Identity and access management issues rose to the number one concern, moving up from second place in 2024, while misconfiguration dropped to fifth. Two artificial intelligence-related threats appeared in the rankings for the first time, including AI-enhanced attacks and AI system compromise. The top eleven threats also include insecure third-party resources, insecure APIs, advanced persistent threats, and inadequate cloud security strategy and governance.

The survey results reveal a significant shift in the cloud threat landscape, with organizations now prioritizing identity protection, artificial intelligence risks, and software supply chains over infrastructure-focused concerns. Security scores ranged closely from 7.95 for identity and access management to 7.45 for system vulnerabilities. The report aims to help organizations make informed risk-management decisions about cloud adoption by providing expert analysis of technical and business impacts, real-world examples, and corresponding security controls across cloud and AI environments.

stories.Headline: EU places ChatGPT, Reddit, Roblox under strictest platform rules
stories.Summary:
The European Union has classified ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine and designated Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms under its Digital Services Act. These three American companies will now face direct supervision from the European Commission and must comply with stricter requirements designed to address risks related to children, election integrity, and public security. The rules apply to services with over 45 million users in the EU, bringing the total number of regulated platforms to 28.

Companies failing to meet the new requirements within four months face fines up to 6 percent of their annual global revenue. Reddit reported 57.2 million EU users in July, while Roblox has 46.6 million. OpenAI stated it would prepare to meet ChatGPT's additional obligations, and Roblox welcomed the designation, emphasizing safety's importance. This designation adds another regulatory layer for ChatGPT, which already complies with the EU's Artificial Intelligence Act.

stories.Headline: Who Writes AI's Rules When Someone Else Owns the Machines?
stories.Summary:
# Summary

South Africa withdrew its Draft National AI Policy in April 2026 after discovering that at least six of its 67 academic references were fabricated, highlighting a broader challenge facing the Global South. The incident underscores a critical debate about who controls artificial intelligence governance and infrastructure. Currently, the United States and China host roughly 86% of global data centre capacity, giving them power to set rules and prices for AI systems worldwide. This concentration of computing power represents what critics call "tech colonialism," where developing nations provide data and demand but lack ownership and control over the technology itself.

BRICS countries and other Global South nations are attempting to shift AI governance away from Western-led standards by emphasizing digital sovereignty and development rights. They are seeking to anchor AI governance within the United Nations rather than OECD-led bodies and have established organizations like the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation. However, meaningful sovereignty requires owning physical infrastructure, not just adopting policies. The article notes that until developing nations build regional computing capacity and chip manufacturing capabilities, they remain dependent on foreign platforms controlled by American hyperscalers or Chinese firms. True sovereignty means choosing dependencies rather than having them imposed.

stories.Headline: AIM Summit 2026 to Bring 50+ CMOs and 600+ Marketing Leaders Together for India's First Dedicated AI-in-Marketing Summit
stories.Summary:
India's first dedicated artificial intelligence and marketing summit will take place in Bengaluru on September 17, 2026, and in New Delhi on September 18, 2026. The AIM Summit will bring together over 50 chief marketing officers from major brands including Paytm, Motorola, KFC, Nestle, and others, along with 600 additional marketing professionals. The event aims to move beyond theoretical discussions about AI and instead focus on practical implementation, real-world applications, and measurable business results for marketing functions.

The summit will feature various components designed to bridge the gap between AI theory and practice. An AI Lab will provide hands-on experiences where marketing leaders can explore actual AI capabilities, while an accompanying exhibition will showcase relevant technology solutions. The event will also include an awards program recognizing organizations successfully using AI for business impact. The summit is being organized in association with CXO Lanes, a community of over 500,000 chief executives and officers across India, and represents an evolution of the organizers' previous marketing conference platform.

Paisabazaar, India's leading financial products marketplace, reports that artificial intelligence now generates approximately 86 percent of new code written on its platform. The company's Chief Technology Officer emphasized that the objective is not to eliminate engineers but to enhance their productivity by automating repetitive tasks. This shift allows engineers to focus on architecture, problem-solving and innovation while accelerating development velocity and enabling teams to pursue a larger product roadmap.

The financial services company is expanding its engineering team despite increased AI involvement, demonstrating its commitment to using productivity gains for expansion rather than workforce reduction. AI-assisted development is integrated throughout the engineering lifecycle, including code writing, testing, debugging and documentation. The company plans to continue deepening AI adoption across both engineering and consumer-facing experiences to expand innovation, improve productivity and deliver more personalized financial services at scale.

stories.Headline: Dyna.Ai Selected as Technology Partner in Hong Kong's GenA.I. Sandbox++
stories.Summary:
Dyna.Ai, a Singapore-based AI company, has been selected as a technology partner in Hong Kong's new GenA.I. Sandbox++ program, marking its second consecutive selection by Hong Kong financial regulators. The sandbox was jointly launched by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Securities and Futures Commission, Insurance Authority, and Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority in collaboration with Cyberport. Out of nearly 100 regional proposals, 36 use cases involving 30 financial institutions and 27 technology providers were chosen, including major institutions like Bank of China (Hong Kong) and Manulife (International), alongside technology partners Google, IBM, and Dyna.Ai.

Unlike earlier programs focused on generative AI banking pilots, Sandbox++ expands across banking, insurance, securities, and pension funds to test Agentic AI systems that execute complex tasks under real-time governance. Dyna.Ai will demonstrate how financial institutions can safely delegate workflow execution to autonomous AI agents while maintaining strict oversight and compliance. The company plans to showcase its solutions and governance frameworks at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh later this year.

stories.Headline: OptiValue Tek Eyes Next Phase of Growth, Expands Focus on AI, Digital Twins and Defence Technology
stories.Summary:
OptiValue Tek Consulting Limited, a New Delhi-based technology company, is moving into a new growth phase with increased emphasis on artificial intelligence, digital twins, and defence technology. The firm has launched ICUDS, an AI-powered counter-drone platform designed to protect critical infrastructure through detection and tracking capabilities. The company received a multi-million-dollar government order through India's Government e-Marketplace to support this expansion. OptiValue is broadening its reach into defence, energy, manufacturing, and logistics sectors as organizations seek better decision-making tools.

The company is also developing digital twins, which create virtual replicas of physical systems to test scenarios and identify vulnerabilities before real-world problems occur. To support this strategy, OptiValue has formed partnerships with Eagle Infrastructure India for intelligent infrastructure development and with SFJ Business Solutions for AI transformation programmes. Chairman Ashish Kumar emphasized the company's goal to connect artificial intelligence with physical systems across defence and critical infrastructure, positioning digital twins as a bridge between digital engineering and operational intelligence for improved organizational resilience.
